question.problem:
Find $\text{E}[\frac{13X}{1-X}],$ given that the continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function

$$
f(x)=\frac{12}{13}(1-x)^{2},\,-\frac{1}{2}\le x\le \frac{1}{2}.
$$
question.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ and a function $r(x),$ the rule of the lazy statistician states that 

$$
\text{E}[r(X)]={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }r(x)f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, we have 

$$
r(x)=\frac{13x}{1-x}.
$$

 

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[\frac{13X}{1-X}] & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }r(x)f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1/2}^{1/2}\frac{13x}{1-x}\cdot \frac{12}{13}(1-x)^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1/2}^{1/2}12x(1-x)\text{d}x \\  & =12{\int }_{-1/2}^{1/2}(x-{x}^{2})\text{d}x \\  & =12{[\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}-\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}]}_{-1/2}^{1/2} \\  & =12[(\frac{1}{8}-\frac{1}{24})-(\frac{1}{8}+\frac{1}{24})] \\  & =12(-\frac{1}{12}) \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$
